gen-dafont-amadeus-fs-nunito: Commanding and wide, Amadeus stretches its words across the line. Nunito is the softer partner, with big round bowls and open line endings that make the pair's mix of muscle and friendliness its strongest quality.
gen-dafont-amadeus-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Pilcrow Rounded sets tight, warm text with tall lowercase and curves that stay open, under Amadeus, whose wide, bold words spread across the line. Pilcrow Rounded over a long passage would read smoothly and snugly, with its generous counters keeping the density friendly.
gen-dafont-amadeus-fs-roundo: Wide, bold and a bit blunt: Amadeus stretches out with rounded strokes and generous gaps. Roundo follows in a moderate lowercase, its small counters staying clear, so a long passage would move along steadily without any clogging.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-graduate: Broad, loud lettering up top, then a sober serif underneath. Amadeus is best at announcing with wide, commanding words, while Graduate is best at holding a dignified line with generous spacing and little difference between caps and lowercase.
gen-dafont-amadeus-merriweather: Chunky rounded lettering meets a cozy, sturdy text face. Amadeus does its best work with bold, uniform strokes, while Merriweather offers a stocky, tall middle band and a soft thick-thin rhythm that rewards a closer look.
gen-dafont-another-danger-fs-literata: Another Danger brings a menacing, commanding look, with Literata beneath it setting sturdy thin lines against slightly heavier ones, like etched glass. A long passage would read as sophisticated and bookish.
gen-dafont-arkhip-archivo: Arkhip floats its wirelike letters well apart. Against that, Archivo's tall lowercase and outward-opening curves give the pair a strongest quality of modern geometry meeting an editorial, approachable voice.
gen-dafont-arkhip-author: Hairline-thin letters drift apart like bent pipe cleaner, and a c opens wide. Author answers with refined, dignified bowls that swell slightly, which is the pair's strongest quality: crisp geometry against a gently narrowing, traditional hand.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-karma: Floating, wire-straight letters meet a trustworthy text face. Karma's modest thick-thin difference gives it a classic feel, but if Arkhip were made small, its spaced-out, hairline strokes would thin out fast.
gen-dafont-arkhip-fs-paquito: Paquito is confident and approachable, with minimal gap between x-height and caps. Arkhip's floating, unvarying wire strokes sit above it, and the strongest quality is that tidy geometry against a friendly serif.
